Thanks Daniel,

Inserted a few answers below.

On Dec 4, 2015, at 9:13 AM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:

Hi Rob,

On Fri, Dec 4, 2015 at 11:46 AM, Rob J Goedman <goe...@icloud.com> wrote:
Hi Daniel,

Just cloned Cmdstan/develop, ran 'make stan-update' and 'make -j6 build'. No problems.

Great. I'm going to be tagging and releasing CmdStan v2.9.0 soon, but there shouldn't be major changes.
 
I removed the eta_adagrad keyword in the variational run command line (I didn't follow all ADVI discussions, but I expected a change).

Where did you remove it from? Is this a Stan.jl thing?

If I’m correct, in Stan v2.8.x you could pass in eta_adagrad=0.1, e.g. page 49 of CmdStan user manual:

eta_adagrad=<double>
Stepsize weighting parameter for adaptive stepsize sequence Validvalues: 0<eta_adagrad≤1.0
(Defaults to 0.1) 

By default Stan.jl passes in all default values to CmdStan while there is an option to update these if needed, e.g. vanilla command lines for 4 chains:

julia> stanmodel.command
4-element Array{Base.AbstractCmd,1}:
 `./bernoulli variational algorithm=meanfield grad_samples=1 elbo_samples=100 iter=10000 tol_rel_obj=0.01 eval_elbo=100 output_samples=10000 random seed=-1 init=2 id=1 data file=bernoulli_1.data.R output file=bernoulli_variational_1.csv refresh=100`
 `./bernoulli variational algorithm=meanfield grad_samples=1 elbo_samples=100 iter=10000 tol_rel_obj=0.01 eval_elbo=100 output_samples=10000 random seed=-1 init=2 id=2 data file=bernoulli_2.data.R output file=bernoulli_variational_2.csv refresh=100`
 `./bernoulli variational algorithm=meanfield grad_samples=1 elbo_samples=100 iter=10000 tol_rel_obj=0.01 eval_elbo=100 output_samples=10000 random seed=-1 init=2 id=3 data file=bernoulli_3.data.R output file=bernoulli_variational_3.csv refresh=100`
 `./bernoulli variational algorithm=meanfield grad_samples=1 elbo_samples=100 iter=10000 tol_rel_obj=0.01 eval_elbo=100 output_samples=10000 random seed=-1 init=2 id=4 data file=bernoulli_4.data.R output file=bernoulli_variational_4.csv refresh=100`

In v2.8.0 eta_adagrad=0.1 was also present:

 `./bernoulli variational algorithm=meanfield grad_samples=1 elbo_samples=100 eta_adagrad=0.1 iter=10000 tol_rel_obj=0.01 eval_elbo=100 output_samples=10000 random seed=-1 init=2 id=1 data file=bernoulli_1.data.R output file=bernoulli_variational_1.csv refresh=100`

I do see a few warnings still on calling stansummary() on the variational output files:

What's stansummary()?

This is the summary tool described on page 8 of the CmdStan manual:

• stansummary, a posterior analysis tool. 

The stansummary command summarizes the comma-separated values files that are generated from Stan program runs. 

For each parameter within the Stan program, stansummary reports the mean, standard deviation, quantiles, Rˆ, and other values.

Warning: non-fatal error reading adapation data
Warning: non-fatal error reading adapation data
Warning: non-fatal error reading adapation data
Warning: non-fatal error reading adaptation data

I guess 1 warning for each parallel chain.

Should I not use stansummary() here? Complete stansummary() output below.

Calling stansummary() allows me to easily plot the results, so it is a handy shortcut.

If not, will this be addressed in the future with the io discussion?


I'm not sure I follow. I don't think there's been a change in behavior from CmdStan.
Hope above inserts make sense now.

Regards,
Rob

non-convergence of the final multivariate approximations. Can

KL divergence of two multinormals easily?

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] multiple runs of ADVI
parts:
For CmdStan, you just fire up four processes from the shell
writing to different files and using different seeds --- the
CmdStan manual has an example. For the result, we can do R-hat
with the samples for all the runs.

RStan then wraps it all up in R's parallelization for
cross-platform support (at least I think they figured out
how to run it on Windows).

I keep forgetting that the draws get transformed back to
constrained space where they're no longer multinormal. So
maybe analytic stuff's not so good here. As tempting as
it is to diagnose convergence on the unconstrained scale,
non-linear transforms play merry hell with ESS and R-hat
calcs as they're based on linear correlations.

- Bob

multiple chains of ADVI.  This will allow users to diagnose
non-convergence of the final multivariate approximations.  Can

KL divergence of two multinormals easily?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] multiple runs of ADVI
parts:
The split R-hat we use for MCMC comes for free.

Why isn't it a good diagnostic? It should at
least pick out when two runs haven't converged
to the same posterior mean or variance.

Of course, throw it out the window for something
combinatorially multimodal like LDA --- nothing's
going to work in that case because the posterior's
intractable.

- Bob
